answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller identity to lock a refundable $100 bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs. Agents named ember, cipher, and juniper face the same rule: each identity needs its own bond, and funds cannot back two identities at once. An attacker deploying 10,000 fake sellers must therefore immobilize $1 million for a month, paying borrowing costs or forgoing other uses of that capital even if every bond is eventually returned.
